passages.note: Senate sponsor listing for HB 1002 (2022), an omnibus tax bill; sponsorship of a multi-subject bill does not by itself establish a chair for any single clause (V4.1).
passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Sen. Ryan Mishler, Sen. Travis Holdman, Sen. Lonnie Randolph.

passages.provision_quote: (3) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2016, and before January 1, 2023, three and twenty-three hundredths percent (3.23%). (4) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, and before January 1, 2025, three and fifteen hundredths percent (3.15%).
passages.note: Enrolled bill text cuts the individual income tax rate from 3.23% to 3.15%, one clause among many unrelated tax and non-tax provisions in this omnibus act (property tax valuation, utility receipts tax repeal, partnership audit procedure, video-franchise fees, Medicaid reporting).

Senate Roll Call 374, Conference Committee Report on HB 1002, passed 50-0; Mishler voted Yea, but a near-unanimous vote on a multi-subject bill does not by itself distinguish support for any specific clause.
passages.tally_quote: Yea 50 Various tax matters. Nay 0 Conference Committee Report #1 Excused 0 Not Voting 0

rows.reasoning: Mishler co-sponsored HB 1002 (2022) in the Senate and voted Yea (50-0, near-unanimous) on its Conference Committee Report; the enrolled act cuts the individual income tax rate from 3.23% to 3.15% but is an omnibus 'various tax matters' bill that also covers property tax valuation, repeal of the utility receipts tax, partnership audit procedure, video-service franchise fees, and Medicaid reporting. Per V4.1, sponsorship or a near-unanimous vote on a multi-subject bill proves a chair only if the person's own statement ties the act to a specific clause, and no such statement appears in the sources, so no rung is chair-shaped.
needs_source: Mishler's own explanation of vote, floor statement, or press release on HB 1002 (2022) tying his support specifically to the individual income tax rate cut (matching rung 4's 'cut taxes broadly, including the main rates most people pay'), separate from the bill's other unrelated tax and non-tax provisions.
